item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
For something as old and as simple as this one is I'm genuinely surprised it's not more iconic in the outer community. It's no 173 or 682, but it gets in, does everything it needs to, and gets out without weighing down the reader with unnecessary details, only genuinely entertaining edge cases. Although I share the complaint with the lol!Foundation at the end, there's a time and a place for lol!Foundation and this is both of these.

My complaints with this one can be reconstructed as compliments. The description is quite a bit wordier than it probably needs to be, but it's cool in a way and actually contributes to this article's charm. There isn't a testing log to demonstrate the effects, but I'd honestly think that a test log would drag this down. The redaction seems cheap, but it's pretty easy to see behind it and it's actually a logical use of redaction.

Easy +1. This is an example of a good Series I skip: short, effective, and simple. I have no doubt that, if this were posted in Series V today, it would survive, unlike most Series I skips from this time period.

item.title: Re: I just realized something
item.content:encoded:
Ok I know I am necroposting here, but I will like to correct u. When something went in from the small end, all its measurement ie length, breadth and height will all increase by 12 times.

For example, a 10 by 10 by 10 cube will become a 120 by 120 by 120 cube.

Simple calculation will show u that the volume increased by 1728 times after going thru the small end ONCE.

item.title: what happens at molecular level ?
item.content:encoded:
After reading this, I can't help but wonder what would happen to matter at a molecular level. For instance, let's say you insert a lump of coal at the small end, and recover it at the other end. You have a lump of coal that's 12 times bigger than the initial one. Now let's say you break a piece in order to analyse it. What happens at molecular level ? Are the molecules 12 times bigger as well, or are there 12 times more molecules ? If that's the case, suppose you rince and repeat the process for N iterations. Would you eventually end up with human sized molecules ?

Another experience : put that lump of coal in a furnace : again, what happens : does the enlarged lump burn 12 times longer than its original "small" counterpart ?

This looks not so much as a funnel as a cornucopia…

item.title: I just realized something
item.content:encoded: The funnel says it's 8 ounces, but it's really 12^3 (1,728) times that size. That's the same factor by which something would be enlarged if put through the small end three times. Coincidence?
Congratulations on the +100 mark, this scip certainly deserves it, being as simple and good as it is.
